records.rec_Title: Magdalena Kremer, Female

details.value: Hamburger, Jeffrey F. « Magdalena Kremer, scribe and painter of the choir and chapter books of de Dominican convent of St Johannes-Baptista in Kirchheim unter Teck ». In Glosses Christopher de Hamel. 2010: "According to the document preserved by sattler, among the nuns who came to kirchheim was ‘ein swester . . . die konde wol textur schriben, und och malen’.11 the author of the document—most likely, given the numerous references to scribal activity, the ‘texturschriberin’ herself—instructed a pair of nuns in calligraphy and illumination at the Dominican convent at Pforzheim during the two days the sisters from silo sojourned there while en route to kirchheim. Later in the same account, this nun is named (or names herself) as ‘Magdalena kremerin, die kam von stroßburg gan syl’ (who came to silo from strasbourg). this is the same Magdalena kremer who wrote the convent’s chronicle and who became prioress of the community in 1495 and served until 1501/1502."

details.value:
Dis bůch het uns geton schriben die erwirdig junckfrow Johanna von Mersperck in dem jor do man zalt von Christi gebůrt m° cccc° xxviij. 
Johanna (Jeanne) von Mörsberg may be regarded either as the scribe of this manuscript or as its commissioner, since tůn schriben can also mean “to have [something] written.” A Poor Clare at the convent of Gnadenthal in Basel, she became, in 1430, a penitent at St Mary Magdalene in the convent “An den Steinen,” where she died in 1450 (?) (Degler-Spengler).

details.value: Les manuscrits de Christine de Pizan ont été écrits par trois mains bien reconnaissables : P, R et X (Christine de Pizan elle-même). Le ms Français 835 a été transcrit, dans sa majeure partie par R, identifié à P. de Cruce : cf.Delsaux, « Profil d’un copiste des manuscrits originaux de Christine de Pisan : P. de La Croix, alias la main R », article à paraître dans Scriptorium. P a copié les ff.441vb, l. 26 à 44vb. La main X a fait quelques corrections : mouche ou restauration sur laquelle l’auteur a réécrit, à l’encre noire, les mots manquants au f.100 : cf.G. Ouy et C. Reno, « Identification des autographes de Christine de Pizan », dans Scriptorium, 34, 1980, p. 221-238.

details.value: Zu lobe und erwurdikeit des almehtigen gottes ouch umb willen eins gemeinen nutzes der andechtigen swester des ordens sant marie magdalene sust genant der orden der ruwerin So hat geschriben dis buechelin Katherina Ingolt ein swester des selben ordens und conuentes zu strossburg mit irer hant grossem ernst flis und arbeit und hat daz volbroht mit der hilff gottes uff sant Thiburcius und valerianus tag Anno domini M cccc lxxxv

In praise and honor of Almighty God, and also for the common benefit of the devout sisters of the Order of Saint Mary Magdalene, also called the Order of the Penitents, this little book was written by Katherina Ingolt, a sister of this same order and convent in Strasbourg, with her own hand, with great diligence, effort, and labor. She completed it with God’s help on the feast day of Saints Tiburtius and Valerian, in the year of our Lord 1485.

f.274v: Hier neempt eijnde dit boeck ghenoempt dat beelt der duechden ghemaeckt (...) duer den subtijlen ende verlichten doctoor bruer peete (sic) dore van Orliens vander predicaren oerdene. Ende nu overgheset uut Fransoijs int duijtschen int minderbrueren clooster tot Gorcum. 
Desen boeck heeft ons ghedaen te scrijven die Eerweerdighe heere Egidius seghers. den welcken selven eerweerdighen heere heeft dien ghetranslateert uut Fransoijs int duijtsche, ende es ghescreven van mij suster marie vander hochstadt voleijndt in die maent Junius Anno M vc ender lxvij Jhesu Maria. flyleaf: tot behoef van convent te Cortenberch. (Other contemporary hand)

f.274 verso: Here ends this book called "The Image of Virtues" made (...) by the subtle and enlightened doctor Brother Peter of Orléans from the Dominican order. And now translated from French into Dutch in the Minorite Friars' monastery at Gorinchem.

This book was done to be written by the Reverend Sir Egidius Seghers. The same Reverend Sir himself translated it from French into Dutch, and it was written by me, Sister Marie van der Hochstadt, completed in the month of June in the year 1567, Jesus Maria. Anna.

Flyleaf: For the use of the convent at Cortenberch. (Another contemporary hand)

details.value: Explicit compendium theologice virtutis (sic). Deo dicimus gratias. Scriptum per Henrietam anno Domini M°CCCLVI (the name and date are difficult to read due to ink smudges). Another mention of the copyist, in her own hand, is found in the upper margin of f.1r: Perscriptum a Henrieta de Lathilliaco, anno LV (not a clear reading), iovis post festum beati Luce (22 October 1355). The reasons for the transcription are explained on the same f.1r:Incipit compendium theologie sancti Thome de Aquino, hic subscriptum interlineariter, ne pargamenum sit occiosum.

Explicit Compendium Theologicae Virtutis (sic). We give thanks to God. Written by Henrietta in the year of our Lord 1356 (the name and date are difficult to read due to ink smudges).

Another mention of the copyist, in her own hand, is found in the upper margin of f.1r: Written by Henrietta of Lathilliaco, in the year 55 (not a clear reading), on Thursday after the feast of Saint Luke (22 October 1355).

The reasons for the transcription are explained on the same f.1r: Here begins the Compendium of Theology by Saint Thomas Aquinas, transcribed here interlinearly, so that the parchment may not remain idle.

value.title: Paris, Bibliothèque nationale de France, Latin 11969

details.value: Hugo Ripelin, Compendium theologicae veritatis, written between the lines and on the margins of a codex containing biblical texts from the 12th century. The space intended for the gloss, which was left blank, was occupied by the new text. The dimensions of the manuscript (ff.195) are 320x215 mm, the space for the original text is 208x90 mm for 18 lines on a full page. Many of the sheets were partially cut, presumably to make parchment. In 1354, before the new text was added, the codex had belonged to Nicasius, curate of 'Casiacum' (Chezy-sur-Marne, Aisne), as can be deduced from the ex libris on f.195v.The manuscript was later transferred to Saint-Germain-des-Prés (ex libris of the 16th century on f.195v and of the 18th century, with the signature 116, on the unnumbered sheet preceding f.1).

The original text has 18 lines, but the new text, copied by a woman has between 20 and 38 lines. It was copied a century after the original text, in spaces originally left for the gloss. Many sheets are partially cut.

The original text was in two columns and the ruling was done with leadpoint. It has catchwords but not signatures. The text block measures: 208x90mm.

details.value: Das puch ist aussgeschriben worden, do man czalt noch unsers lieben herren Iesu xpi gepurt 1451 iar, acht tag vor sant Maria Magdalenatag. Pit den almechtigen god und...s. Katherina fu"r die schreiberin, die dise legent geschriben hat in ir. Das werd war . Amen.'

his book was copied in the year of our dear Lord Jesus Christ, 1451, eight days before the feast of St. Mary Magdalene. Pray to Almighty God and St. Catherine for the scribe who wrote this legend in her love, so that Almighty God may be praised for it, Let this be true. Amen.

details.value: Presens opus cum alijs XII voluminibus incepit fr. Franciscus Mathie de observantia O.Min. sub vicario provinciali patre utique rev. Iohanne de Lindefelcz apud s. Claram in Bamberga in cenobio seu domuncula confessoris virginum atque sororum s. Clare sub abbatissa Katharina Sensenschmidin Iudoco Cutzenbach confessore bene digno cuius anima requiescat in pace. a. incarn. ... 1498 circa festum assumptionis Marie v. et feliciter determinavit manu propria prememoratus fr. Franciscus presbiterorum minimus in litera non (!) illuminatione reliigatione atque correctione sub rev. p. Iohanne Keller proviciali vicario generosa abbatissa Dorothea Marchionissa patre Frederico Gerberstorfer confessore pro tunc existente utique famoso a. salutis 1501 in vig. festi purificationis Marie immaculate virg. (etc.)

This present work, along with twelve other volumes, was begun by Brother Franciscus Mathie of the Observant branch of the Friars Minor, under the provincial vicar, the reverend Father Johannes of Lindefelcz, at St. Clare’s in Bamberg, in the small monastery or residence of the confessor of the virgins and sisters of St. Clare, under Abbess Katharina Sensenschmid, with the worthy confessor Jodocus Cutzenbach, whose soul may rest in peace. In the year of the Incarnation 1498, around the feast of the Assumption of the Virgin Mary, it was happily completed by the same Brother Franciscus, the least of priests, with his own hand. The work was not (!) illuminated, bound, or corrected under the reverend Father Johannes Keller, provincial vicar, the noble Abbess Dorothea Marchioness, and Father Frederico Gerberstorfer, the well-known confessor at that time, in the year of salvation 1501, on the eve of the feast of the Purification of the Immaculate Virgin Mary (etc.).

Written in North France, probably in the convent that produced the three Cologne manuscripts written by nuns for Archbishop Hildebald of Cologne (785–819) and also the Paris manuscript Lat. 18282 (CLA 5.674). Belonged to Pithou whose autographed notes are in the manuscript. Later the property of Colbert in whose collection it was number 1863, and number 3887.14.14 in the Royal collection.

details.value: Ein Ave Maria om gots willen vor den schryuer want hets oer vake suer geworden. >DD<it Boeck heuet geschreuen Suster gertken opten koeten vor oer aelderen der oer jair getyde is op S. kiliaens hynrick opten koete ende else syn huysvrouwe ende oer kynder Ende sie en begert daer vor niet by sonder toe lesen Dan dat got daer in gelaeuet werde ende den susteren in den ketwich ynt gemeyne reventer toe gebruken Ende nummer mer wtten Conuente toe geuen Want sye heuet dat gespaert ende alle dattet gecoestet heuet betaelt ...

One Ave Maria, for God’s sake, for the scribe, as it was often difficult for her. This book is completed in the year of our Lord, when one wrote 1526, on St. Ambrose’s Day in Lent at eight in the morning, and may God be eternally praised for it. This book was written by Sister Gertken Opten Koeten for her ancestors in their yearly remembrance, particularly for St. Kilian, Henrick Opten Koete, and Else his wife, and for their children. She does not seek anything special in return other than that God be praised through it, and that it be used in the convent for common worship in the ketwich (devotional hours) of the sisters, and never given out of the convent, for she kept and paid for all its costs.

value.title: Berlin, Staatsbibliothek, Germ. f.660

details.value: Deo gratias. Amen. XVIII marcii. Deo gratias. Qui scripsit scribat, semper cum Domino vivat. Vivat in celis semper cum Domino felix. Ego Comina (Comina is erased and substituted with ‘domina Iacoma’ in a different but contemporary hand) scripsi istum libellum cum sua (word erased and substituted with 'mea' in same hand as made the correction above) propria manu. MCCCCLII. E ve pregi per carità che voliati pregare Dio per mi. Finito libro referamus gratia Christo.

Thanks be to God. Amen. 18th of March. Thanks be to God. May the one who wrote it always write, and always live with the Lord. May they live happily in heaven forever with the Lord. I, Comina (Comina is erased and substituted with ‘Lady Iacoma’ in a different but contemporary hand), wrote this little book with my own (word erased and substituted with 'my' in the same hand as made the correction above) hand. 1452. And I ask you out of charity to please pray to God for me. Having finished the book, let us give thanks to Christ.

details.value:
Des annotations et corrections interlinéaires sans doute de la main de la copiste : f.4r, 5r, 33r-34r, 39r, 42r, 44r, 46v-54r ; et d’autres mains : f.41r-43v, 47r-47v. Des annotations marginales de diverses mains : au f.1r, la cote Colbert, la cote Regius répétée deux fois, la cote actuelle, une ligne d’un chant religieux (« Nunctio uere quia misit dominus angelimi »), et des neumes (orisci catalans et neumes aquitains ; on en trouve aussi au f.54v) ; d’autres annotations à connotation religieuse sont à noter aux f.6r, 42v et 54v ; un certain nombre d’annotations sont illisibles ou effacées (f.11r, 22r, 40r et 54r) ; on peut également mentionner un astérisque au f.45r, un « y » au f.49r et, d’une main moderne, « 307 » sur le f.54v. 
Comme l’indiquent C. Jeudy (1974, p. 129-130) et B. Bischoff (2014, p. 128-129) dans leur notice respective, le manuscrit a été copié dans le troisième quart du IXe siècle en France, dans un scriptorium d’influence insulaire, par une copiste du nom d’Eugenia, qui donne son nom dans une souscription rédigée en lettres grecques (mais en langue latine) au f.54r (voir H. OMONT, 1905, p. 15 pour la transposition). Il a peut-être été copié dans le Sud de la France ou en Catalogne, ou du moins s’y est trouvé très vite après sa copie, car la main légèrement postérieure à la première (fin du IXe siècle) qui ajoute les carmina des f.54r et 54v est caractérisée par des traits wisigothiques et des neumes d’Aquitaine et orisci catalans ont été notés sur les f.1r et 54v vers la même période.

This is the list of those whose names have written this booklet out of charity. Our honorable father, Mr. Philips Nycholaes, may God be his reward. Sister Beatrix Noeys, Sister Margarete Bont, Sister Janne van den Velde, Sister Marie van Hansbeke, Sister Katherie Tymmermans, Sister Maria Meerts, Sister Margarete Joerdaens, Sister Janne Colijns, Sister Anne Joerdaens, Sister Rijckmoet van Zelken, Sister Maergarete van den Rade. In the book of life, their names are all recorded.

details.value: f.184v-185r: "Completus est iste libellus orarius anno domini M cccc lxxviii ipso die Sancti Ambrosii episcopi. Quem scripsit Soror Wendelmodis Roltemans ad instanciam carissime neptis eius Leve Ter Bruggen honeste matrone. Et Soror Agnes Martini illuminavit. Sancti moniales monasterii ordinis sancti Benedicti ad Sanctam Katharinam In Syloe prope Groenyncgen Urbem inclitam et opulentam in frysia. Eundem orarium prefata Leve Ter Bruggen tamquam entenium[?] memorabile propinando dedit illustri et honesto viro Johanni De Valle rosarum Alias Vanden Roesendael"

f.184v-185r: "This little prayer book was completed in the year of our Lord 1478, on the very day of Saint Ambrose the Bishop. It was written by Sister Wendelmodis Roltemans at the request of her dear niece Leve Ter Bruggen, an honorable matron. And Sister Agnes Martini illuminated it. The holy nuns of the monastery of the Order of Saint Benedict at Saint Catherine in Syloe, near the renowned and prosperous city of Groningen in Friesland. The aforementioned Leve Ter Bruggen, as a memorable gift, gave this prayer book to the illustrious and honorable man John of the Valley of Roses, also known as Vanden Roesendael."

details.value:
f.1r: "desen psalter hoert thoe int convent den susteren tot Sinte katarinen dael binnen hasselt gelaten van onser ierster onder moeder suster katarina vander molen zeliger ende heeften gescreven met haerre properre hant ende sal vortaen bliven geleent vander eenre onder moeder op dander nu ende vortdaen" 
f.250r: "desen souter es op sondage ghescreuen men en machs niet vercoepen mer hi sal der heileger ermer ghemeynten hoeren di niet en hebben ende dien werdelijc ende reynlijc verwaren"

f.1r: "This psalter belongs to the convent of the sisters of Saint Catherine's Valley in Hasselt, left by our first prioress Sister Catherine Vander Molen, may she rest in peace, and it was written with her own hand. It shall henceforth remain lent by one prioress to another, now and in the future."

f.250r: "This psalter was written on Sunday. It cannot be sold, but it shall belong to the holy poor community who do not have it, and it shall be kept worthy and pure."

details.value: Due to the rebinding of the manuscript in the 17th/18th century, the original quire structure is no longer clearly discernible. The modern foliation skips one leaf after fol. 116 and does not take into account the new front and back flyleaves. The soiling of fols. 106r–110v and the change of scribe at fol. 106r suggest that the final part of the manuscript was added to the codex only at the time of rebinding. During this process, fol. 107 was incorrectly sewn: it should in fact follow fol. 118.

Decoration: Red headings, underlining, and emphasis strokes; from fol. 106r onward paragraph marks. Mostly two-line Lombard initials with simple floral ornament and tendril work. On fols. 1r, 43r, and 75r: six-, seven-, and four-line Lombard initials on a floral ground with light brown acanthus-leaf tendrils ending in multicolored blossoms, extending into the upper and outer margins.

Dorothea von Hof (1458-1501)
Dorothea ( Dorathe ) von Hof (born 1458, last mentioned in 1483), who was close to the St. Gallen Dominican Sisters , aged 16 in 1474 with a J erg (Georg von Hof?) married, 1477 conventual of a monastery that is not known with certainty, perhaps the St. Catherine's Monastery in St. Gallen, of which she is a possible patron

12 historiated initials, each incorporating round engraved medallions (later coloured), catalogued by Lehrs.
They follow the Passion cycle:

* f. 61r: Last Supper (In coena domini)
* f. 75r: Christ on the Mount of Olives
* f. 78v: Arrest of Christ
* f. 83r: Mocking of Christ
* f. 87v: Christ before Pilate
* f. 91v: Flagellation
* f. 97r: Crowning with thorns
* f. 103r: Carrying of the Cross
* f. 143v: Christ on the Cross with the two Marys
* f. 152r: Entombment (out of chronological order)
* f. 168r: Deposition from the Cross
* f. 183r: Resurrection

These historiated initials, along with numerous decorated initials (inventoried in CMD-CH III), are enhanced with rich, colorful borders in the classic style of Books of Hours.

Additional decoration:

* 1–2 line red and blue Lombard initials
* rubrication throughout

details.value: Min liebe schwoͤster bit gott fu̍r mich […] [kleine Rasur] Cordula von schoͤnnow beger ich von dir

large ox head with staff and diagonal bar, without eyes or nostrils, with very small ears; the line continues upward past the ears. It is quite similar to Gerhard Piccard, Wasserzeichen II (1966), no. 253, though that example is dated later (1504–1506, Augsburg). At least two variants of the motif appear in this manuscript (see fols. 116–117, where the ears and skull differ).

details.value: Soror Jutta de alfter persoluit istum librum cum suis expensis et elemosynis. Orate pro ea et pro quibus intendit deuote et soror loppa de specula perfecit scribendo liniando notando illuminando quam non excludatis ex cordibus vestris nex non ex oracionibus vestris deuotis anno domini mcccl maximam pestilencia ubique existente.

Sister Jutta of Alfter paid for this book with her own expenses and alms. Pray for her and for those for whom she devoutly intends [her prayers], and Sister Loppa of Spiegel completed it by writing, ruling, noting, and illuminating. Do not exclude her from your hearts nor from your devout prayers, in the year of our Lord 1350, when the great pestilence was raging everywhere.”

f.325: Die episteln hat zu dewchs gemacht der erwiendig geistleich herr maister hans amman aus der weissen aw pey rafelspuerkch den geistleichen jankchfrawn vnd swestern zu den himelparten zu wienn da er dann prior ist gewesen mer dann xx jar dem fot genedig sey. f.325:
“The Epistles were translated by the venerable and spiritual Master Hans Amman from Weissenau near Rafelspuerkch for the spiritual virgins and sisters at the Himmelspforten convent in Vienna, where he served as prior for more than twenty years. May God be gracious to his soul. The Epistles were later copied by Sister Magdalena, whom Almighty God and His beloved Mother Mary hold in their care.”

f.360:
“In the year of our Lord 1468, on the Feast of the Conception of Our Lady, during Advent, this book was completed. It belongs to the Himmelspforten convent in Vienna and was written by Sister Magdalena Panholezin. Pray to God for her with an Ave Maria. Thanks be to God.”

This book was written by Sister Katerina Gudhmundi and Sister Anna Girmundi, each for their half share.

This book was commissioned by Sister Elseby, the daughter of Gyrd, for the convent when she was serving as the cantor. It was written on parchment purchased with the silver belt gifted by her maternal aunt, Mistress Kristin Björn Nielson, which was valued at 24 marks. details.value:
Quire signatures 1–11 appear on the first and last folio of each quire, though they are frequently torn away.

Many folios are heavily damaged and have been repaired with pasted strips cut from other written paper. These preserve fragments of German texts, including:

* Fol. 1: “…gen Onolspach schicken… verporgen sol sein man pricht sie all…” (”…send to Ansbach… should be kept hidden… they break them all…”).
* Fol. 95: an account.
* Fols. 96–97: various fragments of a charter.
Decoration consists of red Lombard initials, occasional corrections marked by red or black cancellations, and drawn pointing hands (manicules) in the margins.
Musical notation appears on fols. 27v, 29v, 89r, 91v, 94r–95r, and 148v.

The Schelm von Bergen family of Wildenberg provided two Cistercian nuns for the convent of Seligental in the 15th–16th c.: Magdalena (attested 1464–1471) and Amalie, d. 1561 as the last abbess (M. details.value: Vollend zu/o/ lob vnd eren / Maria vnd got dem heren / Vnd zu/o/ andau"cht aller maist / Margreten Vesslerin sie hayst. / Ain werde schwester lobesan /Zu/o/ Wilperg in dem stetlin clan / Wel sie bestetgen gottes gwalt / Mit all irn schwestern ju"ng vnd alt. / Wa sy ir gebet vff messenn / Dyss buchlins schryber nit vergessen / Das gschriben ist im iar fu"rwar / Tu"ssend funffhu"ndert verczehen iar / Am abend Magdalene zart / Der all ir su"nd vergeben ward / Wel vns erwerberben (!) gottes segen / Hie vnd dort daz ewig leben. / Amen. / 1514.

Completed in praise and honor / Of Mary and God the Lord /
And in deepest devotion above all / Margreten Vesslerin is her name. /
A worthy and praiseworthy sister / From Wilperg, in the little town nearby, /
Who confirmed God’s power / With all her sisters, young and old. /
When they offer their prayers during Mass, / Let them not forget the scribe of this book, /
Which was written in truth in the year / One thousand five hundred and fourteen, /
On the eve of tender Magdalene / Who was forgiven all her sins. /
May she secure for us God’s blessing / Here and there, eternal life. /
Amen. / 1514.

details.value:
Writer of the main parts: Sister Barbara von Rottenburg in the Dominican monastery Maria-Reut(h)in (Fiala/Irtenkauf p. 84)
Based on the documents used for binding, this (collective) manuscript originates from the Dominican convent of Reutin. According to G. Piccard’s watermark analysis, it was not begun before 1515 and was completed by around 1529.
The main scribe of its primary sections is Sister Barbara von Rottenburg of Reutin (Gand No. 175), who identifies herself in a manuscript she authored (Cod. theol. et phil. oct. 31, f.64r). She is considered the primary scribe of Reutin from around 1488 to 1534. Her works include:
• Cod. theol. et phil. qu. 77 (1488-1492),
• Cod. theol. et phil. oct. 31 (1492),
• Cod. brev. 27 (1511),
• Cod. brev. 73 (1521),
• Cod. theol. et phil. qu. 49a-b (1524),
• Cod. brev. 49 (1529),
• Cod. theol. et phil. oct. 33 (1534).

The writer has also written her name at the top of each page. On 227 r there is also a coat of arms in addition to her name, which is exceptionally placed at the beginning of the layer in the lower edge of the page: red field with a recessed chevron left in the parchment background and three quinces (?) in yellow ( Schraut , Fig. 5);

details.value:
25 paper leaves (ff. 1–14, 47–48, 153–154, 243, 246–252) added in 1674
* Final quires (mixed parchment and paper) are disordered
    Quire signatures in red at the end: I–XXII
    Occasional bifolium signatures (a–e) in brown ink

Rubrication throughout
* Cadels at verse openings, many with mask motifs

Fleuronné initials

* Numerous initials with large-bud fleuronné in red and blue
* 5 large decorated initials with:
    * leaf-spiral fleuronné
    * framed borders in pigment with gold and silver leaf

⸻

Initial Decoration (Detailed)

Smaller initials (responsories)

* Letter bodies split red/blue with varied shaft cut-outs:
    * curved, serrated, stepped, or stamp-like
* Interior fields divided into cells or medallions
* Filled with:
    * large-bud fleuronné
    * floral motifs
    * geometric patterns (checkerboard, zigzag, scales)
* Some motifs left in parchment tone for color contrast
* Occasionally rectangular framing extends into outer field decoration
* Decoration extending into margins is relatively restrained

⸻

Large initials (major feasts)

For:

* Easter
* Palm Sunday
* Pentecost
* Trinity
* Beginning of the Proprium de sanctis

Features:

* One (f. 16r): blue ground, gold vine scrolls and oak leaves
* Others: red/blue split letters with:
    * dragons (spitting foliage, intertwined, forming faces)
    * once: dragons replace rounded shafts entirely

Backgrounds:

* Divided by gold bars into compartments
* Filled with:
    * leaf-spiral fleuronné (red, blue, brown)
    * gold/silver medallions with red rosettes
    * oak leaves and dragons

Borders:

* Three-sided frames with gold bars
* Vine scrolls with:
    * ivy leaves or oak leaves
    * gold acorns or buds
* Birds painted in margins (except one case)

Condition:

* Gold and silver worn; silver oxidized black

11 lines of text with Metz neumes on a five-line staff
    * F-line in red

details.value: 219 r: Explicit hoc opus psalterii per me Barbaram Gretzingerin de Lindow conventualem monasterii nomine Berg anno domini milesimo (sic) quadringentesimo quinquagesimo quarto

Numerous cadels (penwork initials)
* Numerous small fleuronné initials
* 13 large decorated initials

Initials for antiphons and versicles:

Each begins with a one-line-high initial (covering a four-line musical staff + text), usually in a rectangular form:

* Black cadel with a red central stroke
* Left side: looped “rucksack-like” extension
* Interior fields: left in parchment tone, filled with acanthus-like or ornamental motifs, often with hatched areas
* Frequently includes heads or half-figures on the far left
* Right side: contour line with regularly spaced groups of three or four pearls

Psalm Initials

* Psalms begin with mostly 3-line red Lombard initials (rarely 2 lines)
* Decorated with similar contour lines and internal acanthus motifs
* Interiors sometimes highly abstract
* Frequent use of hatched areas

⸻

Major Decorated Initials (12 Psalms)

Unusually, 12 psalms are marked with large (4–9 line) decorated initials:

* Some correspond to liturgical divisions:
    * Psalms 1, 26, 38, 68, 109 → liturgical eightfold division
    * Psalms 51, 101 → Gallican division
* Others (21, 45, 59, 73, 85) do not match known systems

Color schemes:

* Mostly blue-red initials
* One red-green split initial (56r) with stamped or toothed cut-out shapes
* Others: monochrome blue initials

Interior decoration:

* Checkerboard and stripe patterns dominate
* Checkerboards filled with:
    * floral motifs (cross-flowers, star-flowers)
    * diamonds and triangles in alternating red/blue
* Stripe patterns composed of acanthus vines
* Complex geometric arrangements (e.g. Psalm 73: symmetrical grid; Psalm 59: combined pattern system)

⸻

Figural Elements

* Two initials (71r, 86r) contain monster figures in the letter body or interior field
* Example: a large blue fleuronné initial P (206v) with acanthus-filled interior (Office of the Dead)

⸻

Border Decoration

* No uniform system
* Contour lines sometimes form rectangular frames
* Spandrels filled with:
    * acanthus
    * floral stems
    * geometric squares
* Occasional floral extensions and leaf clusters
* Rare use of bud-fleuronné (e.g. Psalm 1)

details.value: 19 fleuronné initials (with pen drawing). The 14 main sections of the first text (summary, introduction, one for each of the 12 brothers) begin with 8- to 13-line red initials, the inner fields of which all contain short tendrils with differently lobed leaves in black outline and sparse internal drawing on a red cross-hatched background (1 ra top, 1 vb , 39 ra ), with the exception of the D on 84 rb , which is filled with a sheaf of buds. Occasionally, grotesque faces in profile appear opposite each other (67 ra ). Star blossoms and S-ornaments with thickened ends are usually left out of the letter bodies, but profile leaves and trifoliate leaves are also occasionally included (26 vb ). The spandrels of the rectangular frames made of narrow strips with short curved sections are often filled with trifoliate and small motifs, occasionally also on cross-hatching. The frame moldings and the left shafts may be decorated with arched friezes (26 vb , 39 ra ) and frequently, at intervals, with short, fan-shaped bundles of rays. Some initials have downward extensions, usually short, consisting of rows of tapering beads bordered by thin lines (1 ra , 1 vb , 39 ra ).

A large compilation combining saints’ lives from the Legenda aurea with the Vaderboec.
Selections include (abbreviated list):
	•	St Longinus (f. 1r–1v)
	•	St Patrick (1v–3v)
	•	Passion of Christ (3v–11v)
	•	Secundus (11v–13r)
	•	St Marcellus (13r–13v)
	•	St Vitalis (13v–14r)
	•	St Peter “the new martyr” (14r–22r)
	•	St James the Apostle (22r–38r)
	•	Gordianus & Epimacus (28r–28v)
	•	Nereus & Achilleus (28v–30r)
	•	Pancras (30r–31r)
	•	Urban (31r–32r)
	•	Petronilla (32r–32v)
	•	Peter the Exorcist (32v–33v)
	•	Primus & Felicianus (33v–34r)
	•	Barnabas (34r–37r)
	•	Vitus (37r–38v)
	•	Quirinus (38v–39v)
	•	Gervasius & Protasius (39v–41v)
	•	The Seven Sleepers (41v–45r)
	•	Pope Leo (45r–45v)
	•	The Seven Brothers (45v–46v)
	•	Theodora (46v–49r)
	•	Margaret (49r–51v)
	•	Praxedis (51v)
	•	Apollinaris (51v–53v)
	•	Christina (53v–55r)

Vaderboec (f. 55v–213v):
Lives of: Achadrus, Macarius, Pachomius, Simeon Stylites, Iheronimus troest, Lupitinus, Pelagia, Eufrosia, Copres the priest, Helenus, Mary of Egypt; plus three short exempla (206–218).

details.value: Summus honor celi / Filius ipse ipse pater / Hoc opus explerunt / Inde sibi veniam / Qui te sustulerit / spes grata Maria fideli / remanes in virgine mater / Aleith Claricia querunt / te venerando piam / hunc anathema ferit.
Mater Ide Lifmundis fecit hec scribi. anima eius requiescat in pace.

The greatest honor of heaven,
the Son Himself, the Father Himself,
completed this work.
From Him, may forgiveness
be given to whoever carries you.
O gracious hope, Mary faithful,
you remain a virgin mother.
Aleith and Claricia seek you,
venerating you, O pious one.
This [text] invokes a curse upon [him who acts against it].
Mother Ida Lifmund had this written. May her soul rest in peace.

details.value: Und das sey also zu lob und zu er got dem almachtigem, Marie und allen heiligen und den menschen zu nuz [?] und zu underweisung. Und aus haissen der erwierdigen geistleichen frawen Ludmille, priorin, meiner mueter und frawen, ich swester Barbara, verlupte der regel sand Augustin und der ordnung und statut Praemonstratensium zu Pernegck hab geschriben das gegenwuertig puech mit aygner hant, das gemacht und gepredigtt hat der hoch gelert maister Gorig von Giengen zu Wien. Und hab das volent am fritag nach sand Bricten tag, des heiligen pischolff [sic] und peichtigner nach Christi gepüerd tausent vierhundert und im newn und funfzigisten jar etc. Die schreiberin pitt zu lon ain Aue maria. Durich gots willen

And may this be for the praise and honor of Almighty God, Mary, and all saints, and for the benefit and instruction of people.
And at the command of the venerable spiritual lady Ludmilla, prioress, my mother and lady, I, Sister Barbara, professed of the Rule of Saint Augustine and of the Order and statutes of the Premonstratensians at Pernegg, have written this present book with my own hand, which was composed and preached by the highly learned Master Georg of Giengen in Vienna.
And I completed it on the Friday after St Brictius’ day, in the year of Our Lord 1459.
The scribe asks as reward one Ave Maria, for God’s sake.

details.value: Zu lob und er got dem almachtigen, Marie und allen heiligen und dem menschen zu underweisung, und aus haissen der erwirdigen geistleichen frawn Ludmille, priorin, meiner lieben muetter und frawn, ich swester Barbara, verluepte der regel sand Augustin und der ordnung und statutt Praemonstratensium zu Pernekch, hab geschriben das gegenwuertig puech mit aygner hant, das gemacht und gepredigt hat der hach gelert maister Gorig zu Wien, und ich hab das volentt an dem nagsten tag nach Colomanni des heiligen m[artyre]r. Die schreiberin pitt zu lan ain Ave Maria umb ir meue die sy hat gehabt mit dem schreiben

To praise and give glory to Almighty God, to Mary, and to all the saints, and for the instruction of humanity, and from the desire of the venerable spiritual lady Ludmille, prioress, my dear mother and lady, I, Sister Barbara, devoted to the rule of St. Augustine and to the order and statutes of the Premonstratensians at Pernegg, have written this present book with my own hand, which was composed and preached by the highly learned Master Gorig at Vienna, and I completed it on the next day after the feast of St. Coloman the martyr. The scribe asks you, as an act of charity, to say an Ave Maria for her soul, for the effort she put into writing.

Dit boeck waert gheynt. Int jaer der gheboerten ons liefs heren ihesu xpristi. Doen men screef duyssent vier hondert ende sevenensestich Op der heiligher glorioser maghet ende mertelerssen sinte dympnen dach. details.value: f. 530v: Gratias Deo et eius matri benedictae virgini Mariae completum Gheertrudis virginis. 1468.
The copyist frequently uses Greek letters for quire and register numbering.

The decoration is rich and carefully executed:
	•	On f. 1r, the page is framed and contains a decorated initial; within the frame is a small miniature of St Augustine holding the civitas Dei.
	•	Space is reserved in the lower margin for a coat of arms.
	•	Large foliate initials on gold backgrounds open major sections.
	•	Smaller initials in blue and red are filigreed in red and purple.
	•	Paragraph marks are in blue and red; titles and running titles are written in red ink.

details.value: f.302: An dem 1316 iar von christes gebort. Is ditz büch erzüget. Von der hoch-geborn vrowen Elzebeten der werden zwire kuninginnen. zu einem ewigen zügnisse iris namen und allers geschlechtes fürsten und kunige om welch closter ditz büch wirt gegeben daz men ir da ewicliche gedenke zum ersten der di da tot sin daz di slafen in Gotes fride und zu der exigen freude kumen. di da noch leben daz sich die freuwen selde und lanklebens; der nach-kümelinge daz si in tusent geslechte wachsen. Amen.

“In the year 1316 after the birth of Christ, this book was produced by the noble lady Elisabeth, descendant of two illustrious queens, as an eternal testament to her name and that of her entire lineage of princes and kings. Whichever monastery receives this book, may she be eternally remembered there. First, for those who are deceased, may they rest in God’s peace and come to eternal joy. For those who are still living, may they enjoy happiness and long life. For their descendants, may they flourish for a thousand generations. Amen.”

Pray to God for her and [to] Mary with one Ave Maria. She was glad from the heart that she wrote [it]. Thanks be to God. Amen.
This was composed by the venerable spiritual father Felix Lessmaister Fabre, to the praise of God and Mary, and for our benefit and good.

This book was written on the feast day of Saint Vincent of the Order of Preachers, in the year one thousand four hundred and ninety-five, by Sister Susanna of Sinzendorf. Pray to God for her with an Ave Maria. Amen.

details.value:
1. Godfrey of Admont (ff. 1r–156r)

Sermons for the Temporal Cycle, Saints, and Apostles

ff. 1r–68v

* Sermon for Advent Sunday
    “The hour has now come for us to rise from sleep…” (Hora est iam nos de somno surgere).
* Sermon for Christmas
    “Behold, now the fullness of time has come. Christ has come! The expected offspring has been born…”
* Sermon for Septuagesima Sunday
    “Who is this who has moved you to such disdain and hatred?”
* Sermon for the Purification of the Blessed Virgin Mary
    “After the days of Mary’s purification had been fulfilled…”
* Sermon for the Annunciation
    “Rejoice, full of grace…”
* Sermon for Palm Sunday
    “Let this mind be in you…”
* Sermon for Easter
    “If you have risen with Christ…”
* Sermon for the Ascension
    “Do not be astonished that I said to you…”
* Sermon for Pentecost
    “When the days of Pentecost had been completed…”
* Sermon on the Holy Spirit
    “The disciples were gathered together…”
* Sermon for the Nativity of St John the Baptist
    “Great praise, faithful joy…”
* Sermon for the Feast of Saints Peter and Paul
    “Today we celebrate the solemnity of Peter and Paul…”
* Sermon for the Assumption of the Blessed Virgin Mary
    “The Assumption of Mary fills all heaven with joy…”
* Sermon for the Nativity of the Blessed Virgin Mary
    “Blessed is she who believed…”
* Sermon for the Translation of St Benedict
    “Blessed is the man who delights in wisdom…”
* Sermon for the Annunciation
    An exhortation to celebrate the feast fittingly.

⸻

2. Sermons on Wisdom

ff. 68r–80r

Sermones de tribus sapientiis (“Sermons on Three Kinds of Wisdom”)

Beginning:

“Blessed is the man who abides in wisdom…”

⸻

3. Sermons and Expositions

ff. 81r–83v

* Sermon for Pentecost
* Sermon on the Twelve Fruits of Charity

⸻

4. Sermons on the Lord’s Prayer

ff. 84r–91r

Sermones in oratione dominica

Beginning:

“Our Father who art in heaven…”

⸻

5. Miscellaneous Sermons

ff. 93r–156r

Contains numerous sermons including:

* Palm Sunday
* Passion Sunday
* First Sunday after Christmas
* Purification of Mary
* Annunciation
* Visitation
* Nativity of Mary
* Nativity of Christ
* A treatise on the Word (Tractatus de Verbis)
* Sermons on the Incarnation

Notable incipits include:

“How beautiful are thy footsteps…” (Quam pulchri sunt gressus tui)

“Come into my garden…” (Veni in hortum meum)

“The voice of my beloved knocks…” (Vox dilecti mei pulsat)

“Set me as a seal upon your heart…” (Pone me ut signaculum)

⸻

6. Irimbert of Admont

ff. 157r–185r

Exposition on Psalm 19–21

Beginning:

“The heavens declare the glory of God…”

The catalogue cites:

* Thesaurus anecdotorum novissimus IV
* Edition by Ruth

⸻

7. Irimbert of Admont

ff. 186r–214v

Exposition on Psalm 15

Beginning:

“Lord, who shall dwell in thy tabernacle?”

Followed by:

Verses

Beginning:

“Omne quod est nimium vertitur in vitium”

(“Everything that is excessive turns into vice.”)

details.value: f.104v: Hie habend end die constitucion der schwesteren prediger ordens M ccccc xliij Iar daz bis buoch folendet ist vor sant gallen tag von schwester regel kellerin von zürich, die begert ein aue maria: deo gracias.

After the council of the city of St. Gallen lifted the enclosure of the Dominican monastery of St. Catherine on May 2, 1528, and the convent gradually dissolved, only Regula Keller and two sisters remained in the monastery buildings, where she continued to copy the Rule of Augustine and the Constitutions of the Order of Preachers until 1543. The reading of the Rule and Constitutions was emphasized more strongly in Reformed monasteries, in keeping with the nature of the Observance. (men)

details.value: [Istum libellum scripsit nobis utilis ac fidelis soror notstra Mechtildis Wolders ultimo vite sue tempore sancta exigente obedientia necnon pro ampliori devotione circa passionem dominicam habendam. Quo completo obdormivit in domino. Omnes legentes in eo ob speciale ipsius anime refregerium devoto corde dicant: Requescat in pace. Amen.]

This little book was written for us by our useful and faithful sister, Mechtildis Wolders, at the end of her life, compelled by holy obedience, and also for a greater devotion to be had regarding the Passion of the Lord. When this was completed, she fell asleep in the Lord. Let all who read it, for the special refreshment of her soul, say with a devout heart: Rest in peace. Amen.

details.value: Finito libro sit laus et honor Christo Ihesu. Scriptrix (sic) donetur in celis merces scribentis sicut pura oratio legentis precorde pro amore Dei. Quicunque legis hunc librum, ut sis memor mei. Scriptrix huius delicatissimi libri et lectores inveniantur in libro viventium et cum iustis scribantur. Arnen dicant omnia.

When the book is finished, let there be praise and honor to Christ Jesus. May the female scribe (sic) be granted in heaven the reward of one who writes, just as a pure prayer from the heart is offered by the reader for the love of God. Whoever reads this book, may you remember me. May the female scribe of this most delightful book and its readers be found in the Book of Life and be written among the just. Let all say Amen.

details.value:
The inside of the front cover and the endpaper contain fragments of a manuscript similar to the Graduale, the back dirt page belonged to a lectionario or breviario from the 14th century and the inside of the back cover is covered with a fragment of a liturgical parchment manuscript, also from the 14th century. At the foot of this fragment is written:
Qui scripsit, scribat et longo tempore vivat. Amen.
Que me scribebat, Sophia nomen habebat. Explicitly liber iste.

During the period in which the Hs. was created, four bearers of this name have been handed down among the Marienberg choir women: the sexton Sophia Barnstorf and the conventual nuns Sophia von Braunschweig , Sophia von Werle and Sophia von Meinersen 
Around 1510, the Graduale was supplemented (Part II) and then re-bound after identifying the scribe's hand and the binding stamp in the Benedictine monastery of Clus in accordance with the requirements of the reformed liturgy of the Bursfeld Benedictine Congregation. 

In the catalogue of Colophons of the Bouveret, noted as wolfenbüttel 542.

details.value:
Signatures in Roman numerals on the lower margin of the last verso page of each quire: I–XXII.
At the rebinding, the text sequence of the final quires was disturbed; the correct leaf order is: 221r–255v, 259r–266v, 269r–v, 256r–258v, 267r–v.

Numerous historiated initials in body color and fleuronnée initials by four hands.
Hand 1: At the beginning of the offices for feasts of the Lord, historiated initials in body color of varying size (each 1–3 lines of text and music) on gold ground framed by alternating red and blue bars. Letter bodies in uncial form in light violet purple with gray contours and dot patterns; ascenders and descenders end outside the frame in winding terminals with a scarcely differentiated red or green half-palmette leaf. 1v initial A over 3 lines of text and music for the proper of the first Sunday of Advent. The letter body is formed by two two-legged dragons in light purple with blue wings, set axially symmetrically opposite each other, whose necks intertwine above Christ enthroned (Maiestas domini). Christ, with red nimbus, is clothed in a purple undergarment and a blue pallium; he holds a book in the left hand, the right raised in blessing. He sits frontally on a white throne into whose sides the two dragons clutch. In the upper spandrels between letter body and frame are the evangelist symbols of Matthew (man, left) and John (eagle, right); the heads of the lion of Mark and the bull of Luke are inserted into the intertwined tails of the two dragons. 8r initial D over 2 lines of text and music for the office of the Christmas Vigil: in the inner field an angel clothed in brown announces the birth of Christ to a shepherd in a red garment who pastures his sheep on green meadow ground. 10r initial P over 3 lines of text and music for the office of the Christmas Mass: before a stylized stable architecture, over whose roof ox and ass look out, Mary, resting on a white couch, in blue undergarment and red outer garment, holds up the infant Jesus wrapped in light-blue linen; Joseph, identified by a red mantle and Jew’s hat, regards the scene from the right. 48v initial D over 2 lines of text and music for the Palm Sunday office: in the center Christ, wearing a blue undergarment and red pallium, enters Jerusalem from the right on a gray ass. Two inhabitants of the city scatter palm branches or have climbed into a tree waving. 55v initial T over one line of text and music for the washing of the feet with Crucifixion scene, the Crucified himself forming the letter T. 61r initial ligature VD over 3 lines of text and music for the Easter procession: from the left come the three Marys in red and blue garments with ointment vessels to the tomb of Christ, where they are addressed by an angel clothed in white, winged red, and nimbed, standing on green ground with black shading. 67r initial P over 3 lines of text and music for the trope of Easter morning Postquam factus est homo: Christ, clothed in blue undergarment and red pallium and armed with a cross-banner, breaks open the gates of hell, represented as the gaping, toothed maw of a monster with blazing flames, and draws Adam out of the chasm. 76v initial V over 2 lines of text and music for the office of the Ascensio domini: the representation follows the type of the disappearing Christ; Mary (left) and Peter (right), together with five further apostles, surround a grass-covered hill on which the footprints of Christ are visible, while the upper half of the Son of God has already disappeared into a blue wavy cloud band. 77v initial S over 2 lines of text and music for the Pentecost office: in the lower part of the letter field sit, in traditional representation, Mary and the apostles in red, green, and blue garments, while from above the Holy Spirit descends upon them in the form of a dove. Similar decoration is also found in the Marienberg liturgical manuscripts Cod. Guelf. 145.1 Helmst. (mentioned by Härting, 15), 1312 Helmst., and 309 Novi. —
Hand 2: 65v marginal narrative representation of Christ’s descent into hell: Christ, clothed in a blue undergarment and red pallium and armed with a cross-banner, breaks open the gates of hell, represented as the gaping, toothed maw of a monster with blazing flames, and leads Adam and Eve upward. Although the coloring in particular corresponds to the miniatures of the first hand, the rendering of garments and folds, and especially of flesh tones and faces, differ considerably. 67r body-color initial R over 5 lines of text and music for the high feast of the Resurrection: Christ, clothed in blue undergarment and red pallium and armed with a cross-banner, rises from his opened tomb, facing the viewer frontally and raising the right hand in blessing. Before the box-like sarcophagus, two guards armored with chain-mail shirts, surcoats, and iron hats, and armed with spears, are sunk in sleep. —
Hand 3: 53v body-color initial N over one line each of text and music for the gradual responsory in coena domini (CANTUS 505005): on golden background framed with a thin black line stands the red uncial letter without any decoration. In the inner field kneels Christ clothed in dark red garment, with cross-nimbus. —
Hand 4: 59v fleuronnée initial I over the entire height of the text area for the hymn of the blessing of the Easter candle in the Easter Vigil (AH 50 no. 31 st. 1–4, 7 [modified], 9–12): the letter itself is colored red and furnished with bands running parallel from top to bottom in wavy meanders in black, white, and light red tones. It evidently represents the Paschal candle itself, at whose top a bell-shaped container is attached, to which the Holy Spirit in the form of a white dove brings fire from above. The contours of the letter body are furnished with delicate blue fleuronnée ornament in the form of parallel thread-like extensions, buds, notched pearls, and fibrils extending upward and downward to the edge of the page. 60v fleuronnée initial E over two lines each of text and music for the Exultet: the letter body, divided red and blue in complex stamp-like patterns, is filled in the two parts of the inner field separated by crossbars with delicate red vines, growing axially symmetrically from vase-like vessels and ending in round medallions filled with bud-spikes. The letter body is enclosed in a blue frame with bud-fleuronnée, which, like the borders extending over the entire height of the text area, is filled with bud-fleuronnée and set with pearls and fibrils. The upper and lower end of the border are decorated with delicate leaf and floral motifs. — Rubricated, mostly red display majuscules with blue contour strokes, together with others (mostly at the beginning of the sequence strophes and in the Kyriale) executed in cadel-like black and red. At the beginning of the individual offices, alternating red and blue fleuronnée initials with variously curving thread-like extensions and simple ornament of buds and pearls as well as fibrils in the contrasting color. Line fillers in various wave and zigzag forms.
Above each text line a five-line staff with c- and f-clef, c-line yellow, f-line red, with a mixed form of Metz and Gothic chant notation by various hands.

details.value: a.d. etc. etc. (14)56 completus est liber iste per me sororem inutilem Alheydem Kalves religiosam ac professam in monasterio Stederborch. pro quo sit Deus benedictus in secula. Pacienciam habete quia male scripsi in anno meo 73 cum magno labore in cenobio Wynhusen in expulsione monasterii nostri. Oretis deum pro me unam angelicam salutationem vel Requiem eternam in xpi amore.

“In the year 1456, this book was completed by me, Sister Alheydem Kalves, an useless religious and professed in the monastery of Stederborch. For which may God be blessed forever. Have patience, for I have written poorly in my 73rd year with great labor in the convent of Wynhusen during the expulsion of our monastery. Pray to God for me, one angelic greeting or eternal rest in the love of Christ.”

details.value:
The expulsion of the Steterburg convent (or part of it) to the Cistercian monastery of Wienhausen, mentioned by the writer, is not documented in any other historiographical or documentary sources.
The liturgical texts following the Windesheim custom and the Commemorationes of the house and order patrons James, Christopher and Augustine prove that the codex was intended for the writer's home convent, the Augustinian canonry of Steterburg, which had been reformed in 1452 according to the Windesheim customs. — On March 18, 1572, it was transferred with the other Steterburg codices to the court library in Wolfenbüttel.


The codex consists of the leaves of at least three palimpsested manuscripts. One of these is a breviary with the office of St. Ansver, which points to an origin in the dioceses of Lübeck, Ratzeburg, Schleswig, or Schwerin

details.value: Dasz puch gehört in die sacristdey tzu Santtha Claren. Es ist geschriben worden do man zeit MV hundert vnd xvij jar. Es ist geschriben worden von einem armen swesterlein s. Claren orden Got zu lob vnd der hoch gelobten iunckfrawen Maria vnd sant Claren meiner lieben Mutter zu eren. Und wer es prachen (brauchen) wirt, der gedenck mein auch mit einem Ave Maria oder mit einem Requiem, swester Anna Newperin.

“This book belongs to the sacristy of St. Clare. It was written in the year 1517. It was written by a poor little sister of the Order of St. Clare, to the praise of God and in honor of the most highly praised Virgin Mary and St. Clare, my dear mother. And whoever makes use of it, may they also remember me with an Ave Maria or a Requiem — Sister Anna Newperin.”

A collection of manuscripts, written primarily on paper, which can be localized to Bamberg. The first part of the manuscript contains a German mirror of salvation. Erasmus Sternhals is identified as its writer in a colophon. The work was probably made for the Bamberg canon Georg von Löwenstein. This is indicated by the depiction of a kneeling canon and several coats of arms on f.56r. The German-language biography of the Holy Bishop Otto, which is bound in afterwards, also refers to Bamberg. It was written down by two Bamberg Poor Clares and completed in 1483. The third work in the collection is a life of Saint Catherine, dated 1488 and also written by a woman.

details.value: The colophon «Iohannes Roderici me fecit» appears on five pieces

3 quinions, a bif., 8 quinions, a quaternio (originally a quinion), 3 quinions, a quaternion, a ternion and a half, and finally a bif.with two single f.s. The last three fascicles have undergone certain displacements, and the correct order of the pages should be f.152, 166, 167, 157, 158, 161, 159, 160, 162, 165, 153-156, 163,164 and 168.

value.title: Burgos, Santa María la Real de Las Huelgas, Ms. 11

details.value:
The Las Huelgas archivists have recently changed the signature of this codex. When Nicolas Bell published his essay in 2004, the codex still bore the signature «MS IX»; today it bears the signature «MS 11".
The main corpus of the manuscript was copied by only one scribe (Scribe A). As noted by Higini Anglès, the calligraphic work of this scribe is characterized by a high degree of irregularity and inconsistency, as well as by frequent changes of pen and ink.

ca. 1300. ca. 1300 for (Dittmer, 1960; Muntané, 2001); 1325 with additions from the late 1330s onwards (Anglès, 1931; ca. 1318-1325, with additions from the 1330s onwads Bell); 1340s principal scribe with additions during the 1340s and/or 1350s by Johannes Roderici and other scribes (Catalunya, 2016)

details.value: Era ’l sicondo di vespar sonato/ nel glorioso giorno che concepta/ fu l’umil Vergin sancta et benedecta/ per chui ’l primo peccar fu ristorato./ A octo giorni del mese ultimato la faticata penna asciutta et necta/ alquanto riposai et con herecta/ mente l’ora vigesima uscì dallato./ Sonavan gli anni del nostro signore/ cinque cinquanta quattrocento et mille/ quando Maria di Matheo cimatore/ finì copiare el testo et le postille/ di questo clar poeta almo, et de core/ che ’nfino al ciel mandò le sue faville./Laus Deo sit semper benedictus.

The second hour of the evening had sounded on the glorious day of the conception of the humble Virgin, holy and blessed, who was free from original sin. On the eighth day of the last month I gave some rest to my weary pen, dry and clean, and the twentieth hour came forth alongside with upright mind. The year of our Lord 1455 was sounding when Maria daughter of Matteo the cloth-shearer finished copying the text and commentary of this poet, renowned and noble, and with a heart that sent its sparks as far as heaven. Praise the Lord, may He always be blessed.

value.title: Oxford, Bodleian Library, Canon. Ital. 285

details.value: Quires are numbered with small roman numerals in the lower inner margin on the last leaf, quire two unnumbered.

Eight 4- to 8-line historiated initials on ff. 1, 55, 97, 98, 119, 169v, 173, 196. Approximately fifteen small ink drawings in the lower margin attached to a descender in the last line of text. Three- to eight-line gold initials with red pen decoration. Several Psalms now begin with 2- to 11-line red or blue initials with contrasting pen decoration, all probably cut from the same manuscript and glued in. Psalm 30 on f. 60 begins with an 8-line blue, pink and gold initial. 1- to 2-line alternately red and blue initials. Red rubrics, calendar with KL monograms in red and blue. Charts and tables. Several initials with protective silk veils.

Written in North-east France or possibly Cologne, as script and ornamentation in the type developed by the nuns of Chelles suggest; the MS has close affinity with the group of three MSS of St Augustine (Cologne, Dombibliothek 63, 65, 67) written by nuns for Hildebald, Archbishop of Cologne (785–819). Belonged to St Faron, Meaux, till the French Revolution, then to Gosselin, later to Remusat, at whose sale it was bought by Messrs Payne, the London booksellers, in 1833.

Origin North France, doubtless Chelles. The peculiar uncial and the decoration connect this MS with the group represented by the famous Sacramentary, Vatic. Regin. Lat. 316 (CLA 1.105). On f.1 is added in Anglo-Saxon script saec. VIII–IX Charlemagne's Letter to Abbot Baugulf of Fulda, and on f.260 a library catalogue, perhaps of Würzburg (see CLA plate). Belonged to St Kilian's of Würzburg certainly by the ninth century, as is shown by the entry on f.1v ('. . . faciat eum sancto Kiliano restitui'). The same page has the Würzburg ex-libris saec. XIII. Acquired by Archbishop Laud before 1638.
Ascribed to Chelles by Bischoff, to Jouarre by McKitterick.

value.title: Chelles Abbey, Benedictine, Chelles, France, 660

In the name of Lord (Jesus) (Christ) [then 'ella' crossed out] and of the glorious Virgin Mary, mother of God, and of Lord Saint John the Baptist, on the day of whose conception this book was begun, the 24th day of September 1488.

This book belongs to the nuns of the Paradiso, copied by me Sister Raffaella with much effort and hardship. And it is the eighth that I have copied, all for the spiritual consolation of my sisters in (Christ), and I do not believe I will copy more except for the Corona of the monks, which I have started in another volume. And if the letter is rustic, the author and the words are worthy, and therefore it should be regarded.
Amen. Finished on the 23rd day of June 1496

details.value: Finito libro isto. Laus et gloria sit domino Iesu Christo. Iesus. Ego soror Angela indigna serva domini nostri Iesu Christi scripsi manu propria hoc collectarium. Deus sit laudatus et pro me deprecatus. Qui scripsit scribat semper cum domino vivat. Vivat in Coelis semper cum domino felix. Facta fine pia benedicat virgo maria.

This book is finished. Praise and glory to our Lord Jesus Christ. Jesus. I, Sister Angela, unworthy servant of our Lord Jesus Christ, wrote this breviary with my own hand. May God be praised and prayed for me.

Deus sit laudatus et pro me deprecatus. Qui scripsit scribat semper cum domino vivat. Vivat in Coelis semper cum domino felix. Facta fine pia benedicat virgo maria."

Suor Angela has been identified as Angela de’Rucellai, Dominican nun of San Jacopo di Ripoli (Levi D’Ancona, Miniatura e miniatori, 11) or as another copist from the same monastery, suor Angela Miniberti or Angela Mineberti (Pini Gruppo di codici, 267-268) Latham states: “This manuscript, also called the Manuale, contained all the prayers, the antiphonals, and the hymns, used by the nuns in their religious services.
Bradley I 38: a nun of the monastery of St. James or Ripoli. Her family name was Miniberti

details.value: Al nome di Dio, a dì 4 d'aprile 1484. Questo o ritrato a mia chonsolatione delle prediche di maestro Mariano romano, di quaresima, in Santa Maria del Fiore in Firenze. Se ci fusi manchamento, sarebe mio difetto: non arei tenuto bene a mente. Io Margherita figliuola di meser Tommaso Soderini o scritto questo di mia mano. Chi lo legie prieghi Idio per me. Se gli è scritto bene, è stato dono di Dio e Lui ringratio. Tutto el bene vien da Dio, tutto el male son io
Di maestro Mariano. Al nome di Dio, a dì 4 di marzo 1488 [1489 in stile comune]. S'io dicho bene, è dono di Dio, s'io dicho [le ultime due parole riscritte] male, son io che o pocha memoria.

In the name of God, on the 4th day of April 1484. This I have copied for my consolation from the sermons of Master Mariano the Roman, preached during Lent in Santa Maria del Fiore in Florence. If there are errors, it would be my fault: I did not keep them well in memory. I, Margherita, daughter of Messer Tommaso Soderini, wrote this with my own hand. Whoever reads it, pray to God for me. If it is written well, it was a gift of God, and I thank Him. All good comes from God; all evil is from me.
Of Master Mariano. In the name of God, on the 4th day of March 1488 [1489 modern style]. If I speak well, it is a gift of God; if I speak badly, it is I who have little memory.

details.value:
in red or reddish-sepia ink, much faded, f.369 bottom of column of text: “[O]* llaude e gloria dello omnipotente Dio e della gloriosa vergine Maria et di sancto Benedetto, P.N. è finito parte di questo libro, cioè capitoli 40, per mano di suora Paula, indengna serva di Yesu Christo, a consolatione di chi lo leggerà, e a chi piacerà, farà prece a dio con quello affetto di carità col quale essa l’à scripto con licentia della sua superiora.” 
f.370 colophon continues at top of column of text: “Nell’anno della salutifera incarnatione del Nostro Signore Yesu Christo Mccccc90 e a dì X del mese di settenbre. Finis.”

"f.369 bottom of column of text: "To the praise and glory of the Almighty God and of the glorious Virgin Mary and of Saint Benedict, P.N., part of this book is finished, namely chapters 40, by the hand of Sister Paula, unworthy servant of Jesus Christ, for the consolation of those who will read it, and to whom it may please, she will pray to God with that affection of charity with which she wrote it, with the permission of her superior."
f.370 colophon continues at top of column of text: "In the year of the salutary incarnation of Our Lord Jesus Christ MCCCCXC, and on the 10th day of the month of September. End."

details.value: Anno domini M.CCC. L.IIII. in Aprili wart diz selebu/o/ch gemachet dem closter ze sante Katherinen bi Friburg von suester Adelheit von Ma/e/ngen der scaffenerin und von suester Agnesen Kemphinen der priolinen und von suester Katherinen von Chu/o/nnehein der selmeisterin... [es folgt ein ausradierter Text, dann:} Anno domini M.CCC.L.IIII.IIII. idus Aprilis scriptus est liber testamentorum nostrorum a Johanne de Constancia sacerdote. Omnes orate pro eo amen. HKOLHagenmaeier 1988 p. 180-181

“In the year of our Lord 1354, in April, this book of wills was created for the monastery of St. Catherine near Freiburg by Sister Adelheit von Maengen, the steward, Sister Agnes Kemphin, the prioress, and Sister Katharina von Chounnehein, the cellarer. [A section of the text is erased.]

In the year of our Lord 1354, on the fourth Ides of April [April 10], this book of wills was written by John of Konstanz, a priest. Pray for him, all of you. Amen.”

Also, this book was written in Maastricht in the enclosed sisters' house at Meerssener Dries. And it was completed on Saint Christina's day. details.value:
Approximately 20 hands or textual sections can be distinguished. Various forms of Bastarda script are used. Since some scripts resemble each other closely, the number of hands may in fact be smaller, and some differences may be explained by different writing phases or circumstances.

As shown by a number of scribal notes, the manuscript was written in a female convent, most likely in a Dominican nunnery. This is suggested not only by internal content-related criteria, but especially by the fact that the first demonstrable owner was probably a Dominican nun at St. Catherine’s in Nuremberg, or alternatively at Maria Medingen

details.value:
On the final folio of several quires, catchwords or remnants thereof appear repeatedly (88v, 100v, 112v, 124v, 192v, 216v, 228v, 268v). It remains unclear whether catchwords were originally present throughout and were lost through trimming, or whether they were only employed by certain scribes in the sections they produced.

The manuscript is a plainly designed utilitarian volume. The texts or sections written by different hands are mostly rubricated, but to very different degrees. Often only the beginning and/or end of texts or text sections, or the transition between larger passages, are rubricated, while the remaining running text is not. Accordingly, rubrication is absent in longer sections: 44v–50r; 52r–54v; 56v–75r; 78v–83r; 84v–93r; 94r–102r; 103r–111r; 112v–116v; 117v–125v; 126v–130v; 131v–136v; 150r–153; 155–160r; 167v–170v; 257v–275v; 276r.

For the most part, rubrication therefore does not appear to have been carried out later in a single, unified process, but rather during the production of the various parts or texts of the manuscript—thus, in many cases probably by the scribes themselves.

In addition to red headings and rubricated capitals or initial letters of textual units, there are occasionally underlinings in red (especially for nomina sacra), as well as chapter and paragraph signs and corrections or deletions in red.

Simple red initials, without decorative ambition, mostly two to four lines high. At the beginning of the text on 1r, a four-line initial was planned but not executed. On 131r, there is a red D-initial, in whose interior field—appropriate to the text, a letter by Heinrich Seuse—the Christogram (Ihs) is written in red. On 233r, a red I-initial extends across most of the height of the page.

details.value: Folio 148v: one scribe: Sister Katherina of Deytzisaw (colophon, dated November 14, 1494, and petition for remembrance 148 rb–vb ) or S katherina (156 va )

On f. 7rb, a historiated E-initial in opaque colour painting, extending over thirteen lines: in front of the blue letter body, which stands on a rectangular, matte rose-violet, ornamented ground, St Catherine, turned to the left, holding a lowered sword; at her feet, the wheel. In the inner field of the initial, a flowered meadow below and punched gold leaf above. From the upper corner of the E, scrolling vines wind along the upper and outer margins.

The remaining opaque-colour initials, among them one particularly emphasised by its size (13 lines) and the elaboration of its vine ornament (f. 2rb, preface), consist of letter bodies with interlace, gem-like, or other ornament, set against an almost square framed ground decorated with floral motifs. The vines are more slender and sinuous, often elongated (frequently within the narrow intercolumnar space), rather than voluminous; as initial extensions they may be short or long and sweeping (f. 10v), or form a vine-staff supported by short initial tendrils (e.g. f. 87vb), occasionally also appearing as an independent branch beside the text column (f. 90ra). In addition, in some instances, flowers and gold pollen are executed in opaque colour painting.

Colours:
Brilliant blue, light blue, grey-blue, red, green, rose-violet; highlights in opaque white and yellow; gold leaf.

details.value: The decoration appears to have been carried out in two or more phases. The original decoration most likely consisted of rubrication, versals, and colour stroking in red, plain 2-line initials in red or green, 2- and 3-line initials with interior reserved shapes in red or green, and large 7-line parted initials in blue and red. All of these were executed with a matte medium. Later, the reserved or interior spaces of most of the larger initials were coloured with red, blue, dark green and pale yellow pigment in a shiny, raised medium and pen flourishing added in lavender or red. This later decoration was done with little skill or finesse. At the same time, many of the larger initials had their interior shapes filled with circular cutouts of saints, presumably cut from prints and pasted to the page, that were also coloured.

Here ends what the deepest thoughts of the heart reveal, written by hand and with the full use of the body, as will be clearly seen by the eye that examines all. Written with flowers, so let us join illustration with text. All this was done and completed by the servant alone in the cloister of Meding, situated near Luneburg. I confess that I belong to the Cistercian order and use the name known to all, called Elisabeth of Winsen. To my own glory and to the glory of Christ, in the year one thousand, four hundred, and ten, with ten added and sixty-three with five combined, on the venerable feast day of Christ, by the command of the venerable Lord Provost Tylemann of Bavensted, and for the sake of ministering to the needs, for the love of my beloved friend, Elisabeth of Bavensted.

details.value:
The text alternates between black and red ink. Red and blue Lombard initials. Many gold initials, two to thirteen lines high, some with blue and red fleuronné decoration, and a few ornamentally split.
With 133 miniatures and historiated initials, this manuscript has the richest decorative programme among the surviving Medingen manuscripts.

The decoration includes angels, saints, biblical figures, Medingen nuns, the Easter Lamb, the risen Christ, scenes from the Resurrection, Christ appearing to Mary Magdalene, Peter and John at the empty tomb, Emmaus scenes, musical angels, animals, birds, trees, and numerous scrolls with song incipits.

Several images specifically show Medingen nuns, for example on fols. 36r, 41r, 44r, 52r, 97r, 104r, 119r, 126v, and 131r.
The manuscript contains red neumes of the Metz type throughout. At the beginning they are nearly diastematic, but later they become imprecise and no longer observe pitch spacing.

details.value:
The script and illumination of the manuscript are attributed to Sibilla von Bondorf, nun of the Clarissen Convent in Freiburg im Breisgau (b. c. 1450, d. after 1524), in 1478.

58 full-page miniatures in colours in orange frames (ff. 4r, 6v, 10r, 15r, 17r, 18v, 19v, 20v, 21v, 23r, 24v, 30v, 33r, 42r, 46v, 48v, 50v, 52v, 59v, 61v, 62v, 63v, 65r, 68r, 72v, 74r, 75r, 76v, 85r, 91v, 93r, 103r, 107v, 110v, 119r, 128v, 131r, 132r, 134r, 136r, 152v, 161r, 161v, 164v, 168r, 168v, 173r, 173v, 179r, 179v, 184r, 184v, 186v, 192r, 195r, 196r, 199r, 246v). 14 one or two column-width miniatures in colours (f. 6r, 35v 39r, 44v, 55r, 84r, 104r, 105v, 111r, 116r, 189v, 203r, 247r, 248r). 4 historiated puzzle initials (ff. 4v, 53r, 65v, 160r). Initials with foliate decoration and display script in colours (e.g., f.10v). Flowers and foliate decoration in lower margins in colours (e.g., f. 19r, 44v, 141r, 148v). Puzzle initials in red and blue with pen-flourishing in both colours. Initials in red or blue with pen-flourishing in the other colour or brown. Partial borders in red and blue with foliate decoration. Rubrics and highlighting in red. Cadels.

details.value: p. 329: Finito libro laus sit xpo. Orate pro scriba que scripsit hunc librum nomen eius Elizabeth. 1260 Bey erster frau abbatissin Agnes graddin Preyssing dis grosse ambt buech geschriben worden von kloster frau Elizabetha. 1462 Hat auch eine closter frau Elisabetha Hyttlen das Gradual Buech verfertiget war 35 jahr cantorin.

“With the book finished, praise be to Christ. Pray for the scribe who wrote this book; her name is Elizabeth.
In 1260, under the first abbess, Agnes Graddin von Preyssing, this great office book was written by the nun Elizabeth.
In 1462, another nun, Elizabeth Hyttlen, also completed the Gradual Book. She served as cantor for 35 years.”

details.value: Expliciunt Deo laus omnipotenti-quinque libri de vita et conuersatione sanctorum patrum scripti per manus sororum Aue Trici et Gheeze Ysenoudi in festiuis diebus suis consororibus dilectis in memoriam earum. Finiti anno domini MoCCCCo XLIXo in festo decollationis sancti Johannis Baptiste ante summam missam. Et habebat ad hoc pergamenum sibi ex caritate prouisum de venerabili presbitero domino nycolao Wyt tunc temporis earundem patre spirituali et sibi ipsius spirtualiter ac in domino sat reuerenter dilectio...

Here ends. To God be praise Almighty – the five books about the life and conduct of the holy fathers, written by the hands of sisters Aue Trici and Gheeze Ysenoudi, on their feast days, for their beloved fellow sisters, in their memory. Finished in the year of our Lord 1449, on the feast of the beheading of Saint John the Baptist before High Mass. And for this purpose, she had parchment provided for her out of charity by the venerable priest Lord Nicholas Wyt, at that time their spiritual father and, with great reverence, her spiritual father in the Lord...

details.value: Hec sunt nomina illarum quae scripserunt librum istum. / Gerdrut. Sibilia. Dierwic. Walderat. Hadewic. / Lugart. Derta (or Ota). Cunigunt. Ipse namque scripserunt mo/nasteriensibus dominis quatinus deum pro eis rogent ut a pe/nis eas liberet & in paradyso collocet. Quisquis eis ab/stulerit anatematizatus sit'

These are the names of those who wrote this book: Gerdrut, Sibilia, Dierwic, Walderat, Hadewic, Lugart, Derta (or Ota), Cunigunt. They wrote it for the lords of the monastery so that they may pray to God for them to be liberated from punishment and placed in paradise. Whoever takes it away from them shall be cursed.

value.title: London, British Library, Harley 3099

details.value: f.166r: 'Hec sunt nomina illarum quae scripserunt librum istum. / Gerdrut. Sibilia. Dierwic. Walderat. Hadewic. / Lugart. Derta (or Ota). Cunigunt. Ipse namque scripserunt mo/nasteriensibus dominis quatinus deum pro eis rogent ut a pe/nis eas liberet & in paradyso collocet. Quisquis eis ab/stulerit anatematizatus sit': (a) ff.1v-29v; (b) ff.30r-50v; ff.51r-63v; ff.64r-93v; ff.94r-119v; ff.120r-145v; ff.146r-153r; ff.154r-167v.

The date '1134' at the end of the note is a post-medieval addition, but the names of five of the nuns are found at the end of a manuscript dated 1130 and produced in the same abbey. Moreover, four among them are mentioned in the mid-12th-century necrology of the same house (see Thoma 1951).

details.value: f.55r: Good Syster of your charyte I you pray remember the scrybeler when that ye may wit/i on aue maria or els thys swete word ihesu have marcy on my wreched syster whose name by the marcy of god rj trust"1 shall be wrytyn In the boke of lyfe Good deuote Syster I pray you to lerne thys lesson well of your master our sauyour cryst ihesu that sayth lerne of me for I am mylde and meke in hart and pray for me that I may do and haue the same

"f.55r: Good sister, in your charity, I pray you to remember the scribe when you may, with an Ave Maria or else this sweet word: 'Jhesu, have mercy on my wretched sister, whose name, by the mercy of God, I trust shall be written in the book of life.' Good devout sister, I pray you to learn this lesson well from your master, our Savior Christ Jhesu, who says, 'Learn of me, for I am mild and meek in heart,' and pray for me that I may do and have the same."

value.title: London, Lambeth Palace Library, Ms. 546

details.value: Lambeth Palace Library MS 546 is a collection of devotional material written by a number of late fifteenth- or early sixteenth-century hands. The main contents are 'The xv Sorowes of oure lady' (fos 7v-20v) and the 'golden letany' (fos 34r-51v, with a preface on fos 29r-33v),4 with devotions in English, and prayers in English and Latin making up the rest of the volume. It is with one of these devotions, specifically its colophon, that the present note is concerned.

details.value: An Antiphonal contains the choral parts sung during the celebration of the Divine Office or Mass celebrated by a monastic or other community. This type of choirbook was usually written in large format so that the whole choir could read the music at once. This example was made at the convent of St Klara in Cologne by one of the nuns, Sister Loppa de Speculo. Another surviving leaf records that Sister Jutta paid for the book while Loppa carried out the writing, lining (putting in the staves for the music), notation and illumination 'in the year 1350, when there was a great plague everywhere'. This was one of a series of books produced in the convent. The Abbess, Heylwigis von Beechoven, who had ruled the convent since 1344, is portrayed kneeling by the historiated initial of the Descent of the Holy Ghost on the Virgin and Apostles associating her prayer with this crucial event, when the Holy Spirit came to earth and the mission of the Apostles to spread the Christian revelation began. The prayer of her convent was thus part of the mission.

details.value:
f.36v
Le ms. Français 1176 est un des vingt-cinq manuscrits entièrement copiés de la main de Christine de Pizan. Selon l’ Album Christine de Pizan, ce manuscrit est le plus ancien témoin du texte, daté de 1405. 

Corrections de la main de Christine de Pizan : additions indiquées dans la marge et rapportées dans l'interligne (f.58) ; additions avec signes de renvoi (f.20v, 43, 63) ; au f.76, préparation de la rubrique en écriture cursive. Nombreux mots, souvent déjà exponctués, barrés de rouge. Au verso de la 3e garde de parchemin, table de l'ouvrage ajoutée à l'encre rouge de la main de l'auteur.

Three signature systems: signatures in text ink consisting of a letter and a Roman numeral, signatures in graphite, signatures in black ink. Catchwords. A few holes (see folios 10, 23, 25, 29, 33), a few stains (see folios 2n, 25v, 55v), edge on folios 52 and 54. Rubricated chapter titles. Rubricated incipits and explicits. Latin quotations underlined in red ink (folios 13v, 15v, 16v, 67).

Decorated letters with phylacteries (fols. 13v, 33, 35v, 37v, 39, and passim) and cadels. Uniform dark brown ink for the main text; bright red for the rubrics. Rubrics and corrections are in the same hand as the principal text.

A semi-grisaille illumination, the width of one column, attributed to the Master of the Epistre d’Othéa, so named for his illustration in the copy made for Duke Jean de Berry (ms. BnF, Français 606). Christine de Pizan is depicted wearing a beige robe and a white cornette, seated in her study on a canopied chair, writing in a book at a table covered with pink cloth. The three coats of arms on either side of the window and beneath the arcade have been left blank.

The secondary decoration is by the ornamenter known as “aux brins de fantaisie”, who worked between 1403 and 1406 on eleven manuscripts produced in Christine de Pizan’s workshop.
Frame of gold and blue bands bordered with scrolling vines of blue and gold florets, with four gold bezants and four gold roundels, alternating with gold “hedgehog” leaves.
Framed initials (4 lines high) on gold grounds on fols. 1 and 25; with a blue phylactery wrapped vertically around the “I” introducing the text on fol. 1.
Champ initials (2 lines high) at the beginning of each chapter.
Champ paragraph marks (pieds-de-mouche).

details.value: Dißes buch ist geschriben worden in dem iar da man zalt von der gebürt Christi M CCCC vnd jm LXXXXIII von zweien schwestren sant claren orden des klosters zu Sefflingen, vnd begerent die schreyberin, daz man gotfür sy bitte, sy seyent lebendig oder tod, mit einem Pater noster oder Aue Maria oder Requiem eternam. 1493. This book was written in the year when one counted from the birth of Christ 1493 by two sisters of the Order of Saint Clare of the convent at Söflingen, and the scribes request that one pray to God for them, whether they be living or dead, with a Pater noster or Ave Maria or Requiem aeternam. 1493.
